papers.title: Does the use of shortened stems reduce early femoral complications in total hip arthroplasty using the direct anterior approach?
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The choice of femoral stem design during total hip arthroplasty (THA) through the Direct Anterior Approach (DAA) is critical. Shortened stems offer potential benefits such as bone preservation and reduced stress shielding. This study aimed to compare early complications at one year of follow-up between shortened and standard stems in DAA THA. METHODS: A retrospective monocentric case-control study included patients undergoing DAA THA from 2013 to 2023. Two cohorts were analyzed: 537 THA with standard stems and 346 THA with shortened stems. Three hundred forty-three patients in each group were matched (1:1) based on age, sex, and Body Mass Index (BMI). Two independent observers assessed femoral complications at one year. Femoral stem positioning was measured. RESULTS: . Shortened stems showed a significantly lower rate of femoral complications (1.4% vs. 5.5%, P = 0.005), particularly for the GT fractures (P = 0.006). In the shortened group, stem alignment was neutral in 69% of cases, varus in 27%, and valgus in 4%. CONCLUSION: Shortened stems in DAA THA were associated with a lower rate of femoral complications, particularly fewer GT fractures. Although shortened stems were more often positioned in varus, this did not impact short-term complication rates. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The Advisory Committee on Research Information Processing in the Field of Health (CCTIRS) approved this study on June 4, 2015 (Study ID 15-430). Video Abstract.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文为临床回顾性研究，比较短柄和标准柄在直接前入路全髋关节置换术中的早期并发症，不涉及AI、生物打印、有限元分析或增材制造，与用户研究方向无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical retrospective study focusing on early complications and stem alignment in THA, with no biomechanical modeling, no FEA, no implant design optimization, no AI/ML, and no additive manufacturing.

summary_en.motivation: To compare early femoral complication rates between shortened and standard stems in total hip arthroplasty via direct anterior approach.
summary_en.method: A retrospective case-control study matched 343 patients per group by age, sex, and BMI, with blinded assessment of complications at one year.
summary_en.result: Shortened stems showed significantly lower rates of femoral complications, particularly greater trochanter fractures, despite more frequent varus alignment.
summary_en.validation: Clinical retrospective matched cohort with independent observer assessment.
